card.situation:
AIE-ITS CSO (W6QK ACC-DTA, Dept of the Army) seeks commercial IT solutions to enhance, secure, sustain, and modernize Army Intelligence IT operations CONUS/OCONUS; awards are fixed-price FAR Part 12 or non-FAR agreements under a Dual-Track (continuous white paper / periodic targeted call) architecture.
Reached the owner because NAICS 541512 matches exactly, three relevant past-performance records exist, and SDVOSB status makes the firm eligible on this unrestricted solicitation — but mandatory non-negotiable security eligibility requirements expose critical gaps.
reasons_for: NAICS 541512 matches the solicitation exactly and three past-performance records covering Army IT help desk, cybersecurity, and M365/Azure migration directly align with the CSO's modernization scope [profile: past performance, US Army Corps of Engineers Tulsa District; FAA Mike Monroney; Oklahoma National Guard].

The CSO's 10-year open window (closing September 11, 2036) and Track 1 continuous white-paper submission model mean the firm could re-enter after obtaining a Top Secret FCL without missing a hard deadline [key_dates: proposal_due 2027-09-11; quote: 'This CSO will remain open until September 11, 2036'].

Technical capabilities — 22-person cleared bench, ACAS/Nessus vulnerability management, RMF/ATO documentation, 24x7 NOC, and CMMC Level 2 self-assessment — provide a credible foundation for a future white paper once security eligibility is resolved [907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-7be3bb97].
reasons_against: The firm does not possess a Top Secret Facility Clearance (FCL), a non-negotiable mandatory eligibility requirement verified in NISS before peer-review; the profile lists only Secret-level cleared staff and no FCL of any level [907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-89bd2272].

The firm cannot certify TS/SCI-eligible personnel, a second non-negotiable mandatory screening criterion; failing either criterion means the firm is barred from peer-review and ineligible for award as currently profiled [907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-f0c9ea86].

Four additional eligibility unknowns — FOCI certification, SAM/UEI registration, OCI disclosure, and government invoicing system registration — compound the disqualifying gaps and cannot be resolved from the current profile [907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-c2f1d2f1; 907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-5e8e218c; 907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-51d86e10; 907ad2ce-4389fa0f-p1-514fddcd].

source_quotes: This CSO will remain open until September 11, 2036.

Sooner Systems LLC — Capability Statement
AIE-ITS CSO | Notice ID: 907ad2ce08a243079f41847b51acebe0

Sooner Systems LLC is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) headquartered in Norman, Oklahoma, operating under NAICS 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) — the exact NAICS code designated for this CSO.

We deliver enterprise IT services to federal customers including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Tulsa District, the FAA Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center, and the Oklahoma National Guard. Our relevant contract history spans Tier 1–3 help desk and desktop support, network administration, cybersecurity support, and Microsoft 365 migration and administration — capabilities that directly address the AIE-ITS CSO's objectives of enhancing, securing, sustaining, and modernizing Army Intelligence IT environments.

Our technical bench includes 22 U.S.-citizen cleared staff holding Security+ and ITIL 4 certifications across the team. We operate a 24x7 Network Operations Center (NOC) in Norman, Oklahoma, and maintain ACAS/Nessus vulnerability management capability alongside RMF/ATO documentation experience. Our Microsoft 365 and Azure administration work for the Oklahoma National Guard demonstrates enterprise IT modernization delivery at the state military level. We have completed CMMC Level 2 self-assessment.

Sooner Systems is committed to outcome-oriented, fixed-price service delivery aligned with the Army's direction under this CSO. We welcome the opportunity to discuss how our capabilities map to open Areas of Interest.

SAM Registration: [To be confirmed prior to submission]

reader.scope_summary: The AIE-ITS CSO seeks commercial IT solutions to enhance, secure, sustain, and modernize the global Information Technology environment supporting Army Intelligence operations across CONUS and OCONUS locations at the Project, Activity, or Enterprise scale. The CSO operates under a Dual-Track architecture: Track 1 allows continuous white paper submissions against Open Areas of Interest, while Track 2 issues periodic targeted Calls for Innovative Solutions with strict deadlines. Resulting awards may include FAR Part 12 Fixed-Price contracts or non-FAR agreements, with the government transitioning the enterprise away from rigid, labor-hour execution toward outcome-oriented service delivery.
reader.evaluation_basis: The competitive process follows a streamlined, multi-phased evaluation approach: Phase 1 (Submission of Written Solution Brief), Phase 2 (Presentation/Pitch, if applicable), and Phase 3 (Request for Commercial Solution Proposal). Vendors must first pass mandatory eligibility screening criteria (Top Secret FCL, TS/SCI personnel capability, FOCI certification, OCI disclosure, SAM registration, and responsibility determination) before being eligible for peer-review. The Price Proposal Volume is evaluated for affordability: "The proposed costs must also be affordable to the Government to be considered for award."
quotes: The objective of this CSO is to leverage agile acquisition authorities to enhance, secure, sustain, and modernize the global Information Technology (IT) environment supporting Army Intelligence operations across Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) locations at the Project, Activity, or Enterprise scale.
5.1.3 Mandatory Eligibility Requirements To be eligible for consideration for an award from the AIE-ITS CSO, vendors must meet all of the following non-negotiable security requirements.
a) Facility Clearance: The vendor must possess a valid Top Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) issued by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) at the time of white paper submission.

b) Personnel Clearance: The vendor must certify their capability to provide personnel who are U.S. citizens and are eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret (TS) clearance with eligibility for Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI).

c) Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI): The vendor must certify that they are not under FOCI in a manner that would preclude them from holding a Top Secret FCL and accessing classified information as required by any potential award.
The Price Proposal Volume will be evaluated as follows: Affordability: The proposed costs must also be affordable to the Government to be considered for award.
In order to receive an award – A company must have a Unique Entity ID (UEI) and shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an award.
Contracts or agreements under this authority shall be fixed-price, including fixed-price incentive fee contracts.
A vendor must be determined "eligible" for all Screening Criteria to be eligible for peer-review.
